In 1773, Americans dumped forty-six tons of tea into Boston Harbor.
And the tea was getting cheaper.
Britain had just cut the price of tea. But it kept one small tax on it.
Three ships full of tea sat in the harbor.
The governor refused to send them back. So the colonists held a meeting.
That night, men dressed as Mohawk marched to the docks.
They climbed aboard, opened every chest, and tipped it into the sea.
It took about three hours. Three hundred and forty-two chests.
Britain answered by closing Boston Harbor.
All over a tax on cheaper tea.
